title: Overview
text: Tessera is a hosted job queue for background work. Jobs are JSON payloads delivered at least once to workers over HTTPS.

title: Payload size
text: A job payload may be at most 256 KB. Larger payloads must be uploaded to object storage and referenced by URL.

title: Visibility timeout
text: When a worker receives a job it becomes invisible to other workers for 30 seconds by default. The worker can extend the visibility timeout up to 12 hours with a heartbeat call.

title: Retries
text: Failed jobs are retried 5 times by default. The delay between attempts grows exponentially, starting at 10 seconds.

title: Dead letter queue
text: After the final retry a job moves to the dead letter queue. Dead letter jobs are kept for 14 days before deletion.

title: Scheduling
text: A job can be scheduled up to 90 days ahead with the run_at field. Scheduled jobs sit in the delay tier and count toward the queue quota.

title: Rate limits
text: The ingest API accepts 500 requests per second per project. Requests above the limit receive HTTP status 429 with a Retry-After header.

title: API tokens
text: API calls authenticate with bearer tokens created in the dashboard. A token expires after 180 days unless its owner renews it.

title: Roles
text: A project has three roles: viewer, operator and admin. Only admins can create or revoke API tokens.

title: Regions
text: Tessera runs in three regions: eu-west, us-east and ap-south. A queue lives in exactly one region and cannot be moved after creation.

title: Encryption
text: Payloads are encrypted at rest with AES-256. Connections accept TLS 1.3 only.

title: Idempotency
text: Send an idempotency key with a job to avoid duplicates. Tessera remembers each key for 24 hours per queue.

title: Priorities
text: Every job has a priority from 0 to 9, and 9 runs first. The default priority is 4.

title: Concurrency
text: A queue can cap the jobs in flight with the max_inflight setting. The default cap is 1000 jobs and the largest allowed value is 50000.

title: Pricing
text: The free plan includes 100000 jobs per month. Beyond that, usage costs 0.40 dollars per million jobs.

title: Uptime commitment
text: Paid plans carry a 99.95 percent monthly uptime commitment. Credits are issued automatically when the commitment is missed.

title: Push delivery
text: Push delivery sends each job as an HTTP POST to your endpoint. The endpoint must answer with a 2xx status within 15 seconds.

title: Client libraries
text: Official client libraries exist for Python, Go and TypeScript. The Python package is named tessera-client.

title: Command line tool
text: The tessera command line tool can inspect queues, replay dead letter jobs and tail logs. Install it with brew install tessera or download the binary.

title: Metrics
text: Queue depth and the age of the oldest job are exported every 60 seconds. They appear in the dashboard and on a Prometheus endpoint.

title: Result retention
text: Completed jobs are kept for 7 days so you can inspect results. An admin can shorten retention to 1 hour in the settings page.

title: Batch submit
text: The batch endpoint takes up to 100 jobs per call. A batch is not atomic, so every job reports its own status.

title: Ordering
text: Tessera does not guarantee global ordering. Jobs that share a group_id are delivered one at a time, in arrival order.

title: Support
text: Support tickets on the Team plan are answered within 8 business hours. Enterprise customers get a 1 hour response during outages.

title: Deleting a queue
text: Deleting a queue is permanent and removes every pending job. An admin must type the queue name to confirm.
